To implement a systematic equity trading strategy focused on low-volatility tilting in the Indian market, we will exploit the empirical observation that low-volatility stocks tend to outperform high-volatility stocks over long periods. This phenomenon can be attributed to investor behavior and risk aversion, where investors often undervalue lower-risk assets, leading to their underpriced nature. This persistence is supported by theories such as the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM) and empirical evidence from various markets.

The trading rule would involve constructing a portfolio that systematically selects stocks with lower historical volatility while maintaining a diversified exposure across sectors. Specifically, at regular intervals, we would screen all listed Indian equities based on their 12-month rolling standard deviation of returns. The lowest-volatility stocks would be given higher weights in the portfolio compared to those with higher volatilities, thereby tilting the overall portfolio towards lower-risk assets. This approach aims to capture the excess returns associated with low volatility while maintaining market exposure and diversification benefits.

The signal for this systematic equity trading strategy is the 12-month rolling standard deviation of returns. This metric is computed from daily open, high, low, close prices over a 12-month period for each listed Indian equity. On a given day, candidates are ranked based on their lowest 12-month rolling standard deviations, with stocks having the smallest volatilities receiving the highest ranks. These ranked stocks are then selected to form the portfolio, with higher weights assigned to lower-volatility stocks to tilt the overall portfolio towards lower-risk assets.

The strategy will hold a diversified portfolio of approximately 30-50 low-volatility Indian equities, ensuring sectoral diversification. Positions are dynamically adjusted based on the 12-month rolling standard deviation of returns. Lower-volatility stocks receive higher weights, with no single stock exceeding 5% of the total portfolio value to limit concentration risk. The strategy aims for a maximum drawdown not exceeding 10% over any 6-month period, ensuring risk is managed within acceptable bounds while capturing low-volatility premium.
